name: Sabeen Talwar
languages: Claims Board legal (the formal register of charter law)
equipment: Ballistic weave jacket, Claims Board grey
Claims Board warrant card: Lapse Assessor, Outer Circuit
Data slate with the full Brinehold charter, all seventy-five years of amendments, and the Article 9 register template
Forgery kit (she would say 'document examination kit')
Two sealed Board evidence cases with tamper tags
Business suit, one, and it shows
features: Extra Training (Human Specialist: proficiency in Computers)
Silver Tongue (expertise in Persuasion and Insight)
Rally (bonus action: an ally who can hear her gains 1d6 + 3 temporary HP and may end being frightened; 3 uses per long rest)
Read the Room (after 1 minute of conversation, learn one goal, fear or lie of the person she is talking to; Insight vs their Deception)
Negotiator (once per day, turn a hostile non-combat encounter into a parley if they can hear her)
Corporate Ladder (Corporate feature: she speaks boardroom and budget, can get meetings with mid-level executives and knows where a company's money goes)

personality.traits: Courteous, exact, and very hard to rattle. I quote clause numbers when I'm angry. Under that I am always furious.
personality.ideals: A charter is a promise from the powerful to the powerless, written down. If nobody holds them to it, it's just paper.
personality.bonds: The Board. Underfunded, slow and the only thing in the outer system that stands between a company and the people who live on its rock.
personality.flaws: I used to write charters like this one for the other side. I know every trick in it because I invented half of them, and I'm terrified someone here will find out.

appearance: A tall, composed woman of forty-four in Claims Board grey, black hair in a severe knot, a long face that gives nothing away. She carries a slate everywhere and reads it while walking. Her one indulgence is a pair of ruby earrings, her grandmother's, which she touches when she's lying.
backstory: Sabeen Talwar is the Claims Board's Lapse Assessor for the outer circuit, the only one for nine moons. She is here to witness the charter's end: certify the head count, take the Article 9 register, and sign off on Adaeze Rask's inquest, because a workplace death in the last ninety days of a charter must be reviewed by a Board officer. She has thirty days, no staff and no ship of her own; she came down on the Tern and goes home on the Plainsong. Before the Board, she spent nine years as a contracts lawyer for a Combine subsidiary, and she drafted the 'voluntary relocation incentive' language the Combine is now using to buy out the Stayers. Caspian Rook knows that. He was in the same office. He greeted her at Pad Row like an old friend.
